Both are `Stationery`, active, not test items, have no notes, and were updated on `2026-02-10`; their prices are `8.00` and `12.00` respectively. help.concept: A multi-row insert uses one column contract for several value tuples.
help.hint_1: Both tuples must contain the same number of values.
help.hint_2: Verify only the two rows from this batch.

sourceCheckMessages.multiRowInsert: Add the approved batch with one multi-row INSERT in operations.sql.

try_inserting_multiple_rows_sketch0.runtimeSolutionCode:
-- file: operations.sql
INSERT INTO inventory_items (name, category, price, status, is_test, notes, last_updated) VALUES
  ('Sketchbook', 'Stationery', 8.00, 'active', 0, NULL, '2026-02-10'),
  ('Marker Set', 'Stationery', 12.00, 'active', 0, NULL, '2026-02-10');

-- file: query.sql
SELECT name, category, price, status, is_test, notes, last_updated FROM inventory_items WHERE name IN ('Sketchbook', 'Marker Set')
ORDER BY name;

single-choice-1.title: Purpose of Multi-row INSERT
single-choice-1.prompt: What is the primary advantage of using a multi-row INSERT statement?

help.concept: Multi-row INSERT statements allow inserting multiple rows in one go, which is efficient and reduces the chance of errors.
help.hint_1: Think about how it affects the number of statements executed.
help.hint_2: It reduces the number of separate INSERT statements needed.

options.a: It allows inserting multiple rows with a single statement, improving efficiency.
options.b: It ensures each row is inserted in a separate transaction.
options.c: It automatically checks for duplicate entries.
options.d: It allows inserting rows without specifying column names.

multi-choice-1.title: Pieces of the Taught Multi-row INSERT Pattern
multi-choice-1.prompt: For the explicit-column, multi-row INSERT pattern taught in this course, which pieces are required? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-1.hint: Think about the one shared destination list followed by several row-value groups.

help.concept: This course uses one explicit column list, the VALUES keyword, and multiple value tuples for a reviewable batch insert.
help.hint_1: The shared column list defines the meaning of every tuple.
help.hint_2: A WHERE clause does not belong to an INSERT VALUES statement.

drag-reorder-1.title: Order of INSERT Statement Components
drag-reorder-1.prompt: Arrange the components of a multi-row INSERT statement in the correct order.
drag-reorder-1.hint: Read each piece and arrange them in the order the statement should be understood.

help.concept: The pieces should form a valid statement in a logical order.

fill-blank-choice-1.title: Use a SQLite Default in a Batch
fill-blank-choice-1.prompt: In this course's SQLite runtime, how do you let a column's DEFAULT apply to every row in a multi-row INSERT?
fill-blank-choice-1.hint: The shared column list applies to every tuple in the batch.

help.concept: SQLite applies the column default when that column is omitted from the INSERT column list.
help.hint_1: Every tuple must follow the same shared column list.
help.hint_2: Do not place DEFAULT as an individual value inside a SQLite VALUES tuple.

fill-blank-choice-1.template: To use a column's default value in an INSERT, [blank1] the column from the column list.

single-choice-2.title: Verifying Inserted Data
single-choice-2.prompt: What is the best way to verify that data has been inserted correctly?
single-choice-2.hint: Think about using SQL queries to check data.

help.concept: Using a SELECT query to verify inserted data ensures accuracy.
help.hint_1: Consider what SQL command retrieves data.
help.hint_2: A SELECT query can confirm the presence of new data.

options.a: Run a SELECT query to check the new data.
options.b: Check the database logs for insertions.
options.c: Rely on the success message from the INSERT command.

multi-choice-2.title: Why Defaults Help an INSERT
multi-choice-2.prompt: Which are useful effects of relying on a schema default when a column is intentionally omitted? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-2.hint: Choose effects that come from letting the table provide one routine value consistently.

help.concept: Defaults reduce repeated literals and give omitted columns a consistent starting value; they do not require every column to be supplied.
help.hint_1: A default can make repeated inserts shorter and more consistent.
help.hint_2: A default does not mean every column must be named.

options.a: It reduces repeated literal values in INSERT statements.
options.b: It gives omitted columns a consistent starting value.
options.c: It reduces opportunities to mistype the same routine value repeatedly.
options.d: It requires every table column to appear in the INSERT.

sketch0.title: One VALUES list can add several approved rows
sketch0.bodyMarkdown:
When several rows belong to the same approved batch, one `INSERT` can use one column contract followed by several value tuples.

```sql
INSERT INTO inventory_items (name, category, price, status) VALUES
  ('Shipping Box', 'Stationery', 4.25, 'active'),
  ('Tape Dispenser', 'Stationery', 9.75, 'active');
```

Each tuple creates one row. Every tuple must supply values in the same order as the shared column list.

sketch1.title: Every row in the batch follows the same column contract
sketch1.bodyMarkdown:
A multi-row insert is one statement, not several unrelated inserts placed next to each other. The single column list defines the meaning of every tuple that follows it.

Before running the statement, compare the tuples vertically: the first position should describe the same field in every row, the second position should describe the same field, and each tuple should contain the same number of values.

After the change, verify only the new batch so an unexpected row is easy to notice.

If every row in a SQLite batch should use the same schema default, omit that column from the shared column list so the default applies to every tuple.
